subtopic: Tetravalence of Carbon: Shapes of Organic Compounds
stem:
How many \(\sigma\) and \(\pi\) bonds are present in each of the following molecules?
(a) \(\text{HC}\equiv\text{CCH}=\text{CHCH}_3\)
(b) \(\text{CH}_2=\text{C}=\text{CHCH}_3\)
solution:
(a) \(\sigma_{\text{C}-\text{C}}\): 4; \(\sigma_{\text{C}-\text{H}}\): 6; \(\pi_{\text{C}=\text{C}}\): 1; \(\pi_{\text{C}\equiv\text{C}}\): 2

(b) \(\sigma_{\text{C}-\text{C}}\): 3; \(\sigma_{\text{C}-\text{H}}\): 6; \(\pi_{\text{C}=\text{C}}\): 2.

subtopic: Tetravalence of Carbon: Shapes of Organic Compounds
stem:

(a) \(\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}\)
(b) \((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CO}\)
(c) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CN}\)
(d) \(\text{HCONH}_2\)
(e) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCN}\)

subtopic: Tetravalence of Carbon: Shapes of Organic Compounds
stem:
Write the state of hybridisation of carbon in the following compounds and shapes of each of the molecules.
(a) \(\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{O}\)
(b) \(\text{CH}_3\text{F}\)
(c) \(\text{HC}\equiv\text{N}\)
solution:
(a) \(sp^2\) hybridised carbon, trigonal planar.

(b) \(sp^3\) hybridised carbon, tetrahedral.

(c) \(sp\) hybridised carbon, linear.

subtopic: Structural Representations of Organic Compounds
stem:
Expand each of the following condensed formulas into their complete structural formulas.
(a) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3\)
(b) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{CH}_3\)
solution:
(a) The complete structural formula shows every atom and every bond:

\(\text{H}-\overset{\text{H}}{\underset{\text{H}}{\text{C}}}-\overset{\text{H}}{\underset{\text{H}}{\text{C}}}-\overset{\text{O}}{\text{C}}-\overset{\text{H}}{\underset{\text{H}}{\text{C}}}-\overset{\text{H}}{\underset{\text{H}}{\text{C}}}-\text{H}\)

that is, a five-carbon chain \(\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\) in which the third carbon carries a doubly bonded oxygen and each of the other four carbons carries its full complement of C–H bonds.

(b) A seven-carbon chain with a double bond between the second and third carbons:

\(\text{H}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\)

written out in full as \(\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\), every C–H bond shown explicitly, the two doubly bonded carbons carrying one hydrogen each.
_note: The book prints both solutions as fully drawn complete structural formulas (every C, H and bond line). They are transcribed here in an equivalent written form.

subtopic: Structural Representations of Organic Compounds
stem:
For each of the following compounds, write a condensed formula and also their bond-line formula.
(a) \(\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_3\)
(b) The structure in which a central \(\text{CH}\) carries an \(\text{OH}\) group above it and a \(-\text{C}\equiv\text{N}\) group on each side: \(\text{N}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{C}\equiv\text{N}\)
solution:
Condensed formula:

(a) \(\text{HO}(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2\)

(b) \(\text{HOCH}(\text{CN})_2\)

Bond-line formula:

(a) A six-carbon zig-zag chain drawn with \(\text{HO}\) at one end, a methyl branch on the fourth carbon and a second methyl branch on the fifth carbon (an isopropyl terminus).

(b) A single carbon vertex carrying \(\text{OH}\) above it, with \(\text{NC}-\) on one side and \(-\text{CN}\) on the other.

subtopic: Structural Representations of Organic Compounds
stem:
Expand each of the following bond-line formulas to show all the atoms including carbon and hydrogen.
(a) A cyclohexane ring bearing a branched three-carbon group attached through its middle carbon (an isopropyl substituent).
(b) An unbranched eight-vertex zig-zag chain.
(c) A chain drawn as \(\text{HC}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}_3\) in bond-line form, the \(\text{OH}\) written below the fourth vertex.
(d) Two \(\text{CH}\) vertices joined to each other, each carrying two methyl groups.
solution:
(a) The ring is a six-membered carbon ring; drawing every atom gives a ring of six carbons, four of them \(\text{CH}_2\), one \(\text{CH}\) bearing the side chain, and the side chain itself is \(-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_3\); the complete structural formula shows the ring carbons with their hydrogens and the branch carbon carrying one hydrogen and two methyl groups.

(b) \(\text{H}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{H}\), i.e. an eight-carbon chain in which each of the two end carbons carries three hydrogens and each of the six inner carbons carries two.

(c) \(\text{H}-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\overset{\text{H}}{\underset{\text{H}}{\text{C}}}-\overset{\text{H}}{\underset{\text{OH}}{\text{C}}}-\overset{\text{H}}{\underset{\text{H}}{\text{C}}}-\text{H}\)

(d) \(\text{H}_3\text{C}\) and \(\text{CH}_3\) above, \(\text{H}_3\text{C}\) and \(\text{CH}_3\) below, joined to the two central carbons:

\((\text{H}_3\text{C})(\text{H}_3\text{C})\text{CH}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)(\text{CH}_3)\), each central carbon also carrying one hydrogen.
_note: The stem in the book is FOUR DRAWN BOND-LINE FORMULAS with no text; they are described in words here. The printed solution (a) is on page index 3 and (b)-(d) continue on page index 4.

subtopic: Nomenclature of Organic Compounds
stem:
Structures and IUPAC names of some hydrocarbons are given below. Explain why the names given in the parentheses are incorrect.
(a) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\)
2,5,6-Trimethyloctane [and not 3,4,7-Trimethyloctane]
(b) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\)
3-Ethyl-5-methylheptane [and not 5-Ethyl-3-methylheptane]
solution:
(a) Lowest locant number: the set 2,5,6 is lower than 3,5,7 (the book compares the locant sets obtained by numbering from the two ends), so numbering must begin from the end that gives 2,5,6.

(b) The substituents are in equivalent positions; the lower number is given to the one that comes first in the name according to alphabetical order. Ethyl precedes methyl alphabetically, so ethyl gets locant 3.

subtopic: Nomenclature of Organic Compounds
stem:
Write the IUPAC names of the compounds i–iv from their given structures.
(i) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\)
(ii) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3\)
(iii) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH}\)
(iv) \(\text{CH}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2\)
solution:
(i) The functional group present is an alcohol (\(-\text{OH}\)); hence the suffix is '-ol'. The longest chain containing \(-\text{OH}\) has eight carbon atoms, so the corresponding saturated hydrocarbon is octane. The \(-\text{OH}\) is on carbon atom 3 and a methyl group is attached at the 6th carbon. Hence the systematic name is **6-Methyloctan-3-ol**.

(ii) The functional group present is a ketone (\(>\text{C}=\text{O}\)), hence suffix '-one'. Presence of two keto groups is indicated by 'di', so the suffix becomes 'dione'. The two keto groups are at carbons 2 and 4. The longest chain contains 6 carbon atoms, hence the parent hydrocarbon is hexane. Thus the systematic name is **Hexane-2,4-dione**.

(iii) Here two functional groups, namely ketone and carboxylic acid, are present. The principal functional group is the carboxylic acid group; hence the parent chain will be suffixed with 'oic' acid. Numbering of the chain starts from the carbon of the \(-\text{COOH}\) functional group. The keto group in the chain at carbon 5 is indicated by 'oxo'. The longest chain including the principal functional group has 6 carbon atoms; hence the parent hydrocarbon is hexane. The compound is therefore named **5-Oxohexanoic acid**.

(iv) The two \(\text{C}=\text{C}\) functional groups are present at carbon atoms 1 and 3, while the \(\text{C}\equiv\text{C}\) functional group is present at carbon 5. These groups are indicated by suffixes 'diene' and 'yne' respectively. The longest chain containing the functional groups has 6 carbon atoms; hence the parent hydrocarbon is hexane. The name of the compound is therefore **Hexa-1,3-dien-5-yne**.
_note: Parts (i) and (ii) with their solutions are on page index 10; the solution to (iii) and the whole of (iv) are on page index 12 (page index 11 is Table 8.4).

subtopic: Nomenclature of Organic Compounds
stem: Derive the structure of (i) 2-Chlorohexane, (ii) Pent-4-en-2-ol, (iii) 3-Nitrocyclohexene, (iv) Cyclohex-2-en-1-ol, (v) 6-Hydroxyheptanal.
solution:
(i) 'hexane' indicates the presence of 6 carbon atoms in the chain. The functional group chloro is present at carbon 2. Hence the structure of the compound is \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{Cl})\text{CH}_3\).

(ii) 'pent' indicates that the parent hydrocarbon contains 5 carbon atoms in the chain. 'en' and 'ol' correspond to the functional groups \(\text{C}=\text{C}\) and \(-\text{OH}\) at carbon atoms 4 and 2 respectively. Thus the structure is \(\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_3\).

(iii) A six-membered ring containing a carbon–carbon double bond is implied by cyclohexene, which is numbered so that the double bond lies between C-1 and C-2. The prefix 3-nitro means that a nitro group is present on C-3. The double bond is a suffixed functional group whereas \(\text{NO}_2\) is a prefixed functional group, therefore the double bond gets preference over the \(-\text{NO}_2\) group in numbering. The structure is cyclohexene carrying \(-\text{NO}_2\) at C-3.

(iv) '1-ol' means that an \(-\text{OH}\) group is present at C-1. \(\text{OH}\) is a suffixed functional group and gets preference over the \(\text{C}=\text{C}\) bond. Thus the structure is a cyclohexene ring carrying \(-\text{OH}\) at C-1 with the double bond between C-2 and C-3.

(v) 'heptanal' indicates the compound to be an aldehyde containing 7 carbon atoms in the parent chain. The '6-hydroxy' indicates that an \(-\text{OH}\) group is present at carbon 6. Thus the structural formula of the compound is \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}\). The carbon atom of the \(-\text{CHO}\) group is included while numbering the carbon chain.

subtopic: Nomenclature of Organic Compounds
stem:
Write the structural formula of:
(a) o-Ethylanisole
(b) p-Nitroaniline
(c) 2,3-Dibromo-1-phenylpentane
(d) 4-Ethyl-1-fluoro-2-nitrobenzene
solution:
(a) A benzene ring carrying \(-\text{OMe}\) (\(-\text{OCH}_3\)) and, on the adjacent (ortho) carbon, \(-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\).

(b) A benzene ring carrying \(-\text{NH}_2\) and, on the opposite (para) carbon, \(-\text{NO}_2\).

(c) \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\): a five-carbon chain whose C-1 bears the phenyl group and whose C-2 and C-3 each bear a bromine.

(d) A benzene ring carrying \(-\text{F}\) at C-1, \(-\text{NO}_2\) at C-2 and \(-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\) at C-4.
_note: The book prints all four answers as drawn ring structures; they are transcribed here in words. Problem 8.10 sits at the top of page index 14, i.e. it belongs to section 8.5.4 (Nomenclature of Substituted Benzene Compounds), not to section 8.6 Isomerism which begins lower on the same page.

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem:
Using curved-arrow notation, show the formation of reactive intermediates when the following covalent bonds undergo heterolytic cleavage.
(a) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{SCH}_3\)
(b) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CN}\)
(c) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{Cu}\)
solution:
In each case the curved arrow starts at the bond and points to the atom that keeps the shared pair.

(a) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{SCH}_3 \rightarrow {}^{+}\text{CH}_3 + {}^{-}\text{SCH}_3\) — the bonding pair goes to sulphur, giving a methyl carbocation.

(b) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CN} \rightarrow {}^{+}\text{CH}_3 + {}^{-}\text{CN}\) — the bonding pair goes to the cyanide carbon, giving a methyl carbocation.

(c) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{Cu} \rightarrow {}^{-}\text{CH}_3 + {}^{+}\text{Cu}\) — here the curved arrow points towards carbon, because carbon is more electronegative than copper, so a methyl carbanion is formed.

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem:
Giving justification, categorise the following molecules/ions as nucleophile or electrophile:
\(\text{HS}^{-}\), \(\text{BF}_3\), \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O}^{-}\), \((\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N}\!:\), \(\overset{+}{\text{Cl}}\), \(\text{CH}_3-\overset{+}{\text{C}}=\text{O}\), \(\text{H}_2\text{N}\!:^{-}\), \(\overset{+}{\text{N}}\text{O}_2\)
solution:
**Nucleophiles:** \(\text{HS}^{-}\), \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O}^{-}\), \((\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N}\!:\), \(\text{H}_2\text{N}\!:^{-}\). These species have an unshared pair of electrons, which can be donated and shared with an electrophile.

**Electrophiles:** \(\text{BF}_3\), \(\overset{+}{\text{Cl}}\), \(\text{CH}_3-\overset{+}{\text{C}}=\text{O}\), \(\overset{+}{\text{N}}\text{O}_2\). Their reactive sites have only six valence electrons; they can accept an electron pair from a nucleophile.

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem: Identify the electrophilic centre in the following: \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{O}\), \(\text{CH}_3\text{CN}\), \(\text{CH}_3\text{I}\).
solution: Among \(\text{CH}_3\text{H}\overset{*}{\text{C}}=\text{O}\), \(\text{H}_3\text{C}\overset{*}{\text{C}}\equiv\text{N}\) and \(\text{H}_3\overset{*}{\text{C}}-\text{I}\), the starred carbon atoms are the electrophilic centres, as they will have a partial positive charge due to the polarity of the bond.

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem:
Which bond is more polar in the following pairs of molecules:
(a) \(\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{H}\), \(\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{Br}\)
(b) \(\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{NH}_2\), \(\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{OH}\)
(c) \(\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{OH}\), \(\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{SH}\)
solution:
(a) \(\text{C}-\text{Br}\), since Br is more electronegative than H.

(b) \(\text{C}-\text{O}\)

(c) \(\text{C}-\text{O}\)

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem: In which \(\text{C}-\text{C}\) bond of \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}\) is the inductive effect expected to be the least?
solution: Magnitude of inductive effect diminishes as the number of intervening bonds increases. Hence, the effect is least in the bond between carbon-3 and hydrogen.
_note: BOOK INCONSISTENCY, transcribed faithfully: the question asks for a C–C bond but the printed solution names "the bond between carbon-3 and hydrogen", which is a C–H bond. The molecule has only two C–C bonds (C1–C2 and C2–C3, numbering from the carbon bearing Br).

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem: Write resonance structures of \(\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^{-}\) and show the movement of electrons by curved arrows.
solution:
First, write the structure and put unshared pairs of valence electrons on appropriate atoms. Then draw the arrows one at a time moving the electrons to get the other structures.

\(\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{O}^{-} \leftrightarrow \text{CH}_3-\text{C}(-\text{O}^{-})=\text{O}\)

The curved arrow moves the lone pair on the singly bonded (negatively charged) oxygen into the C–O bond while the \(\pi\) pair of the C=O bond moves onto the other oxygen, so the negative charge is delocalised equally over both oxygen atoms.

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem: Write resonance structures of \(\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CHO}\). Indicate relative stability of the contributing structures.
solution:
The three contributing structures are:

I: \(\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{H}\)

II: \({}^{+}\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{C}(-\text{O}^{-})-\text{H}\)

III: \({}^{-}\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{C}(-\text{O}^{+})-\text{H}\)

Stability: I > II > III

[I: most stable, more number of covalent bonds, each carbon and oxygen atom has an octet and no separation of opposite charge. II: negative charge on the more electronegative atom and positive charge on the more electropositive atom. III: does not contribute, as oxygen has a positive charge and carbon has a negative charge, hence least stable.]

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem:
Explain why the following two structures, I and II, cannot be the major contributors to the real structure of \(\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_3\).

I: \(\text{CH}_3-\overset{+}{\text{C}}(-\text{O}^{-})-\ddot{\text{O}}-\text{CH}_3\)

II: \(\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(-\text{O}^{-})=\overset{+}{\text{O}}-\text{CH}_3\)
solution: The two structures are less important contributors as they involve charge separation. Additionally, structure I contains a carbon atom with an incomplete octet.

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem: Explain why \((\text{CH}_3)_3\overset{+}{\text{C}}\) is more stable than \(\text{CH}_3\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2\), and \(\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_3\) is the least stable cation.
solution: Hyperconjugation interaction in \((\text{CH}_3)_3\overset{+}{\text{C}}\) is greater than in \(\text{CH}_3\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2\), as \((\text{CH}_3)_3\overset{+}{\text{C}}\) has nine C–H bonds. In \(\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_3\), the vacant \(p\) orbital is perpendicular to the plane in which the C–H bonds lie; hence it cannot overlap with them. Thus, \(\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_3\) lacks hyperconjugative stability.

subtopic: Quantitative Analysis
stem: On complete combustion, \(0.246\,\text{g}\) of an organic compound gave \(0.198\,\text{g}\) of carbon dioxide and \(0.1014\,\text{g}\) of water. Determine the percentage composition of carbon and hydrogen in the compound.
solution:
Percentage of carbon \(= \dfrac{12 \times 0.198 \times 100}{44 \times 0.246} = 21.95\%\)

Percentage of hydrogen \(= \dfrac{2 \times 0.1014 \times 100}{18 \times 0.246} = 4.58\%\)

subtopic: Quantitative Analysis
stem: In Dumas' method for estimation of nitrogen, \(0.3\,\text{g}\) of an organic compound gave \(50\,\text{mL}\) of nitrogen collected at \(300\,\text{K}\) temperature and \(715\,\text{mm}\) pressure. Calculate the percentage composition of nitrogen in the compound. (Aqueous tension at \(300\,\text{K} = 15\,\text{mm}\))
solution:
Volume of nitrogen collected at \(300\,\text{K}\) and \(715\,\text{mm}\) pressure is \(50\,\text{mL}\).

Actual pressure \(= 715 - 15 = 700\,\text{mm}\)

Volume of nitrogen at STP \(= \dfrac{273 \times 700 \times 50}{300 \times 760} = 41.9\,\text{mL}\)

\(22{,}400\,\text{mL}\) of \(\text{N}_2\) at STP weighs \(28\,\text{g}\).

\(41.9\,\text{mL}\) of nitrogen weighs \(= \dfrac{28 \times 41.9}{22400}\,\text{g}\)

Percentage of nitrogen \(= \dfrac{28 \times 41.9 \times 100}{22400 \times 0.3} = 17.46\%\)

subtopic: Quantitative Analysis
stem: During estimation of nitrogen present in an organic compound by Kjeldahl's method, the ammonia evolved from \(0.5\,\text{g}\) of the compound in Kjeldahl's estimation of nitrogen neutralized \(10\,\text{mL}\) of \(1\,\text{M}\) \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\). Find out the percentage of nitrogen in the compound.
solution:
\(1\,\text{M}\) of \(10\,\text{mL}\) \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 1\,\text{M}\) of \(20\,\text{mL}\) \(\text{NH}_3\)

\(1000\,\text{mL}\) of \(1\,\text{M}\) ammonia contains \(14\,\text{g}\) nitrogen.

\(20\,\text{mL}\) of \(1\,\text{M}\) ammonia contains \(\dfrac{14 \times 20}{1000}\,\text{g}\) nitrogen.

Percentage of nitrogen \(= \dfrac{14 \times 20 \times 100}{1000 \times 0.5} = 56.0\%\)
_note: The stem and the opening of the solution are on page index 32; the solution completes on page index 33.

subtopic: Quantitative Analysis
stem: In Carius method of estimation of halogen, \(0.15\,\text{g}\) of an organic compound gave \(0.12\,\text{g}\) of \(\text{AgBr}\). Find out the percentage of bromine in the compound.
solution:
Molar mass of \(\text{AgBr} = 108 + 80 = 188\,\text{g mol}^{-1}\)

\(188\,\text{g}\) \(\text{AgBr}\) contains \(80\,\text{g}\) bromine.

\(0.12\,\text{g}\) \(\text{AgBr}\) contains \(\dfrac{80 \times 0.12}{188}\,\text{g}\) bromine.

Percentage of bromine \(= \dfrac{80 \times 0.12 \times 100}{188 \times 0.15} = 34.04\%\)

subtopic: Quantitative Analysis
stem: In sulphur estimation, \(0.157\,\text{g}\) of an organic compound gave \(0.4813\,\text{g}\) of barium sulphate. What is the percentage of sulphur in the compound?
solution:
Molecular mass of \(\text{BaSO}_4 = 137 + 32 + 64 = 233\,\text{g}\)

\(233\,\text{g}\) \(\text{BaSO}_4\) contains \(32\,\text{g}\) sulphur.

\(0.4813\,\text{g}\) \(\text{BaSO}_4\) contains \(\dfrac{32 \times 0.4813}{233}\,\text{g}\) sulphur.

Percentage of sulphur \(= \dfrac{32 \times 0.4813 \times 100}{233 \times 0.157} = 42.10\%\)
_note: The stem begins on page index 33 and continues, with its solution, onto page index 34.

subtopic: Structural Representations of Organic Compounds
stem:

stem:
Classify the following reactions in one of the reaction type studied in this unit.
(a) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{HS}^{-} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{SH} + \text{Br}^{-}\)
(b) \((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HCl} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{ClC}-\text{CH}_3\)
(c) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{HO}^{-} \rightarrow \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Br}^{-}\)
(d) \((\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{HBr} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CBrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\)
_note: BOOK TYPO, corrected to the intended symbol per the transcription brief: in part (b) the printed page sets chlorine's lower-case l as a CAPITAL I, so the page reads "HCI" and "(CH3)2CIC". Verified at 22x against the genuine lower-case l in Ex 8.4(f) ("Cl2CHCH2OH"), whose glyph is an ascender with no top serif while the glyph here sits at cap height with serifs at both ends. Transcribed as Cl.

(b) A \(\text{C}=\text{C}\) in which the left carbon carries \(\text{D}\) above and \(\text{H}\) below while the right carbon carries \(\text{H}\) above and \(\text{D}\) below; and a \(\text{C}=\text{C}\) in which the left carbon carries \(\text{D}\) above and \(\text{H}\) below while the right carbon carries \(\text{D}\) above and \(\text{H}\) below.
(c) \(\text{H}-\text{C}(=\overset{+}{\text{O}}\text{H})-\text{OH}\) and \(\text{H}-\overset{+}{\text{C}}(\text{OH})-\text{OH}\)
_note: FIGURE-DEPENDENT IN THE BOOK: all three pairs are printed as DRAWN STRUCTURES on page index 37 and are described here from the page. In (a) the two bond-line drawings are a five-carbon chain with the C=O on the middle vertex, and a five-carbon chain with the C=O on the second vertex.

(b) \((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{O} + {}^{-}\text{OH} \rightarrow {}^{-}\text{CH}_2\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O}\)
(c) \((\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{Br} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_3\overset{+}{\text{C}} + \text{Br}^{-}\)

_note: FIGURE-DEPENDENT IN THE BOOK: parts (b), (c) and (d) are printed as DRAWN bond-line structures on page index 37 (only (a) is printed as text). They have been read off the page and written as equations here; in (b) the ketone is drawn as a bond-line \(>\!\!=\!\text{O}\) (propan-2-one) and the product carries the minus sign on one of its methyl carbons.
